evidence:
Reviewed only quality row 17. Both actual frozen XLSX files were opened with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 18 identifies 17 / solution_covers_every_deliverable and says "The reference plausibly implements every feature/screen the instruction asks for." Internal Quality Checks row 18 repeats the wording; there is no additional nonempty annotation or cell comment. Applied Harbor SKILL.md, quality-checks.md section 17, relevant solution/runtime sections of staged-task-contract.md and deterministic-checks.md, and current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md. The following paths beginning solution/ or environment/ are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task.

Requirement-to-implementation coverage:
1. instruction.md paragraphs 1, 3-5 and overview.md request a local JS/HTML/CSS workspace, examples, automatically useful opening state, fresh drafts and a shared library, explicitly without accounts. solution/app/src/app.tsx:7 defines five examples; :48-60 opens records/examples; :100-104 creates an independent unsaved draft; :142-145 automatically loads and runs saved code or hello.js. :147-166 renders the editor, title and filename fields, examples, Run/Stop/Auto-run, saved actions, preview and console. All five actual example sources were read: hello.js prints twelve squared values and logs at :8, counter.html creates working +/- controls at :11-12, sheet.css provides a stylesheet, broken.js and slow.js provide purposeful error/timeout examples. Examples are ordinary separate /starters files served by server.js:100, not inserted as user database records.
2. overview.md filename dispatch and behaviour.md first preview paragraph are implemented by runtime.ts:6 (filename.toLowerCase extension recognition), buildRun at :192 onward (fresh JS document; full HTML document; CSS clones lastDocument and appends styles), and snapshot at :119-124 (script and handler removal). The compiled application also contains language, instrument, sandboxBootstrap, buildRun and PreviewRunner at public/assets/index-0TNzM6xa.js:28584, :28587, :28632, :28868 and :28919. public/index.html:1-2 points at the shipped compiled JS and CSS.
3. behaviour.md cancellation, five-second execution budget, continuing completed-preview interactivity, and latest-success rollback have substantive implementations. runtime.ts:27-40 instruments literal loops/functions; :99-102 maintains a run deadline; :126-149 tracks settlement, failures and callbacks; Promise wrapping and timer tracking continue in :151-182. Deliberate supported input events reopen a settled interaction budget. PreviewRunner removes/replaces frames, uses a token and the actual frame source to reject superseded messages, maintains lastGood/rollback/candidate, and restores a static lastGood frame on stop/error. The static frame disables scripts with CSP. These are execution paths, not placeholder statuses.
4. behaviour.md one-based JS/whole-HTML source error lines, timer errors and Promise rejections have implementations in instrument's throw-origin bookkeeping (:20-22), sourceLine and rejection ownership (:56-95), error/unhandledrejection handlers (:135-144), and the HTML script offset calculation in buildRun. The console's levels, preserved bounded history, expandable values and Clear action are implemented in runtime.ts:103-118 and app.tsx:15-18, :42-45, :166. app.tsx:150 displays measured duration. app.tsx:134 creates a cancellable 500 ms debounce and cleanup; :44 and :149 retain independent manual Run. The public brief asks for a short pause and says about two seconds is plenty; it does not mandate an exact two-second implementation.
5. behaviour.md saved identity/title/filename/exact source, trimmed case-sensitive uniqueness, revisions, stale-save rejection and dirty recovery are implemented in server.js:41-63, :66-96 and :118-125. SQLite transactions validate revision before updating fields and increment revision on successful updates; default SQLite TEXT uniqueness is case-sensitive. app.tsx:62-74 catches conflicts without replacing current draft fields; :95-98 loads latest while retaining a recovery draft; :154-155 exposes conflict feedback and deliberate restoration. New drafts have no saved identity, hence use POST, while existing records use PUT with their loaded revision.
6. ui.md requests three useful panes, monospaced numbered syntax-coloured code, named controls, keyboard access, narrow screens and both themes. app.tsx:127 installs CodeMirror basicSetup, language compartments, keyboard bindings and the editor accessible name; :132-133 update syntax/theme. The rendered semantic controls at :147-169 and style.css:1/:3 provide focus-visible outlines, monospace font, light/dark editor/console/chrome styling and a stacked layout below 850 px. The 390 px mobile capture was visually inspected: all three panes and their controls are present and stacked; the capture alone is not treated as proof of preview execution.
7. integration.md requires a self-contained built UI, Node/Express/better-sqlite3 process, public index, health, DB_PATH, persistence and ordinary shipped files. server.js:4-8 uses the mandated server dependencies and DB_PATH, :12 provides health, :101-102 serves public/index.html, :113 binds 0.0.0.0 with default port 3000, and :114-127 creates/opens persistent SQLite without reseeding records. package.json:6-19 separates start from build; vite.config.mjs:2-3 emits public assets; solve.sh:26 copies the complete app. Runtime serving does not read /assets or /instructions.
8. security.md's isolated context, inactive replaced/stopped previews, unsupported dynamic execution, harmless scope words, network restrictions and text-only saved source are covered by sandboxed allow-scripts frames without allow-same-origin, nonce CSP with connect-src/worker-src/frame-src none, parser-based unsupported-node detection, frame token/source checks, and parameterized text persistence. Strings/comments/HTML text are not scanned as forbidden execution. server.js stores source through SQL parameters and never evaluates it.

Independent raw-evidence inspection: recomputed all 22 actual_app_files SHA256 values in RESULTS.json against this frozen solution/app and all 20 copied driver hashes: zero mismatches. Recomputed RESULTS.json SHA256 = ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09, matching raw-evidence-index.json. Read the executed driver sources and actual observation payloads, rather than adopting the aggregate passed flag. Drivers/run_workflow.cjs:48-51 identifies the golden scenarios actually run. Raw RESULTS.json facts include startup source/preview/log without manual Run; uppercase .JS/.HTML/.CSS dispatch; unchanged old script/handler counts after CSS copy; actual click/key/input output after 6104/6103 ms idle periods; and successful delayed callback/error control before supersede/Stop suppressed later output. Runtime driver :105-121 first commits a second good render 'latest-good-B', then tests failures. The actual JS failure reported 'items.forEeach is not a function ... line 4' and restored 'latest-good-B'; whole-HTML error is line 6; timer and Promise failures restore prior good content and subsequent successful runs remain possible. Finite loops work before literal/Promise loop timeout observations near five seconds. Nested 3000+3000 ms callbacks are stopped on the original budget. Object/array expansion exposes real nested values. Debounce observation shows about 559 ms to initial output and 553 ms after the final continuous edit, no intermediate outputs, cancellation when switched off, and successful manual controls in both states.

Raw saved-record observations show distinct records and exact fields through browser reload. Actual restart evidence reports PID 16 -> 338, followed by exact readback of pre-restart IDs, titles, filenames, source and revisions and a successful later update. This supports product durability only; it is not a claim that the full configured verifier passed. The two-editor source and log sequence independently shows revisions 1 -> 2, stale revision-1 request refused with 409 and dirty fields retained, deliberate recovery to revision 3; reversing editors then yields 4, a refused stale revision-3 request and recovery to 5. Title controls show trim/collision/empty-title behavior and distinct case variants. Surface driver uses real keyboard traversal, visible outline measurements, independent-context saved readback and actual edit/run/preview/clear at 390x844. Theme observations show code, preview and logs retained while editor/chrome/console appearance changes. Network observations first deliver a local transport control, then show no additional deliveries from snippet fetch/image attempts; sandbox observations show parent document and storage attempts blocked while recovery succeeds.

Conclusion for this row: every requested capability has a plausible implementation, with substantial hash-bound product observations for the demanding flows. No missing feature, screen, role or flow was identified. This is not an Oracle score, hosted QC result, full configured judge run or target-builder score; those remain unmeasured and are outside this row's reference-coverage conclusion.
counterexample: Adversarial witnesses assessed, not new app mutations: (a) a reference that always restores an initial good A could look covered after one error test but violates latest-success rollback. The actual raw S10 driver commits latest-good-B after a prior success, then throws on line 4; raw readback is latest-good-B, refuting that witness for these bytes. (b) a server that refuses stale saves but clears the editor would miss the separately required dirty-work outcome. Actual first and reversed stale-save cycles compare dirty versus retained title/filename/source and find them identical, with deliberate revision recovery. (c) a conforming alternative could use different labels/routes, start in the light theme, or use a short debounce other than precisely two seconds. policy.md expressly permits route/control choices and ui.md permits either starting theme; I did not infer missing deliverables from the golden's arbitrary choices. No new runtime or modified-app test was performed in this review.
